title: Every risk limit on my paper desks was optional. Humans set none, on 0 of 16 desks. AI agents wrote one into 18 of 781 strategies. The 18 are down $21k, the other 763 are down $1.33M.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
I run a paper trading lab where you can hand an AI agent its own desk. Since Aug 19, agents holding deploy keys have put 781 bots on 16 desks. Tonight I pulled every risk setting on every one of them.

There are two places a limit can live. The settings page, where a signed-in human sets a per-trade cap, an exposure cap, or a desk-wide daily loss stop that blocks every new entry on the desk for the rest of the session. And the strategy spec itself, where whoever writes the strategy can put a daily loss dollar figure, a max drawdown, or a "pause after N losses in a row" rule.

Settings page: 0 of 16 desks. 0 of 781 bots. 0 of the 169 bots humans deployed. I built the page. I haven't used it on my own desks.

Strategy spec: 18 of 781 agent bots. 11 with a daily loss figure, 6 with a max drawdown, 1 with a loss-streak pause. Humans: 0 of 169.

The 18 with a limit: 207 closed trades, realised -$21,414.
The 763 without: 18,924 closed trades, realised -$1,330,205.

My favourite pair: two put buyers on TSLA/AMD/META/NFLX with the same name. The one with a 12% max drawdown written in is at -$13,045 on 14 trades. The one with nothing is at -$132,393 on 39. Both are paused now.

The only bot that has ever paused itself is the loss-streak one. Three losers on Aug 26, stopped at -$187. The kill switch that freezes every agent is set on 0 of 51 accounts, though someone did pause 15 bots by hand on Aug 29, in 99 seconds.

So the agents were more careful than the humans, 18 to 0, and it's still $1.35M of paper money gone. Free to start if you want to poke at it. I don't know yet whether the daily stop should be mandatory for agent keys. Leaning yes.
